story_type: sailboat torn apart in a hurricane far offshore, cargo ship takes the crew off
hook: A hurricane was tearing their sailboat apart, 414 miles out.
narration: Hurricane Julio was tearing this sailboat apart, four hundred fourteen miles northeast of Oahu.
Three men were aboard the forty two foot Walkabout, sailing from Stockton, California, to Honolulu.
The storm took the mast, and the boat started to flood.
A hatch blew away, the pumps could not keep up, and their life raft went overboard.
Winds hit up to one hundred fifteen miles an hour, with thirty foot seas.
A Coast Guard Hercules flew out and dropped pumps and life rafts to the boat.
A plane cannot lift anyone out of the sea, so the Coast Guard leans on passing ships.
The cargo ship Manukai turned two hundred seventy six miles off course to reach them.
Its first try, sending over a life raft, failed. [short pause] The seas were too rough.
outcome: The next morning, the Manukai pulled the sailboat alongside, and all three climbed a thirty foot ladder to safety.
title: Sailboat torn apart by a hurricane
description:
In August 2014, the 42-foot sailboat Walkabout was dismasted and flooding in Hurricane Julio, 414 miles northeast of Oahu, with three men aboard. A Coast Guard HC-130 crew flew overhead, and the containership Manukai diverted and took all three aboard.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 2nd Class Tara Molle, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/354790/sailboat-caught-hurricane-julio
